chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ that he had heard Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) say:

For every Imam there is a covenant binding upon his adherents and followers, and the completion of honoring this covenant and fulfilling their duties well lies in visiting their tombs. Whoever visits them with eagerness for their visitation and affirmation of what they encouraged, their Imams will be their intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting the tombs of the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) defines the 'covenant' (al-'ahd) as a binding spiritual contract fulfilled through the specific act of visiting the Imams' tombs, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a sign of loyalty (wilayah). By visiting with sincere eagerness (tashdiqan) and affirming the Imams' authority, the believer secures the Imams' intercession (shafa'ah) on the Day of Resurrection, linking physical devotion to eschatological reward.
